chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) raised it from them (peace be upon him) that he said to one of his companions,
and he had asked him about the matter to continue in it, and he could not find anyone to consult, so how should he be dealing with it? He said: 'Consult your Lord.'
So he said to him, 'How?' He said to him: 'Intend the need within yourself, then write out two pieces of paper, in one, 'No', and in one, 'Yes', and make these two to be inside two balls of clay.'
Then pray two Rak'at of Salat, and make these two to be behind you.
and say, 'O Allah! I hereby consult You in this matter of mine, and You are the best of the consultants and advisers, therefore advise me with what is correct for me in it and the best safety.'
Then insert your hand, so if it was 'Yes', so do it, and if it was 'No', do not do it. This is how you consult your Lord.'
ai.seo_question: How does one perform the prayer of Istikhara for decision-making according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the ritual of Istikhara as a method of seeking divine consultation (Shawr) when human advice is unavailable, emphasizing that Allah is the best advisor. It prescribes a specific procedure involving writing 'Yes' and 'No' on paper, placing them in clay balls (bunduq), performing two units of prayer, and casting lots to reveal the divine choice. This practice underscores the Shia understanding of Istikhara not merely as supplication, but as a tangible mechanism for receiving guidance, rooted in the concept of Tawakkul (trust in God).

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Muhammad, 
(It has been narrated) raising it, from them<sup>asws</sup> that he<sup>asws</sup> said to one of his<sup>asws</sup> companions,

and he had asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the matter to continue in it, and he could not find anyone to consult, so how should he be dealing with it?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Consult your Lord<sup>azwj</sup>’.

So he said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘How?’ 
He<sup>asws</sup> said to him: ‘Intend the need within yourself, then write out two pieces of paper, in one, ‘No’, and in one, ‘Yes’, and make these two to be inside two balls of clay,
then pray two Rak’at of Salāt, and make these two to be behind you,

and say, ‘O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! I hereby consult You<sup>azwj</sup> in this matter of mine, and You<sup>azwj</sup> are the best of the consultants and advisers, therefore advise me with what is correct for me in it and the best safety’.
Then insert your hand, so if it was ‘Yes’, so do it, and it is was ‘No’, do not do it. This is how you consult your Lord<sup>azwj</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 8. Ali ibn Muhammad has narrated in a marfu’ manner from one of ’A’immah who has said the following: “The Imam, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, said to one of his companions
who had asked about an issue that he wanted to do but did not find any one to consult with. The Imam said, ‘Consult your Lord.’
He then asked, ‘How should I do so?’ The Imam replied, ‘Keep in your mind what you wish to do, then write two pieces of paper, “yes” on one and “no” on the other. Place them inside two balls of clay,
perform two Rak‘at Salah (prayer) and place them under your furnishing
and say, “O Allah, I consult You in this matter and You are the best consultant and advisor. Grant me a sign about that which is beneficial and is of good consequences,”
then take out one of the papers; if it is “yes”, then do what you wanted and if it is “no” then do not do it. This is how you consult your Lord.’”
